title: Revisions to the Entity List
summary:
The U.S. Commerce Department has made two notable export control updates: it’s temporarily easing some licensing requirements that will reduce paperwork for a year, and it’s removing one China-based company from its restricted Entity List while cleaning up several aliases tied to another listing. These changes take effect November 10, 2025.

Who benefits? Exporters and supply chain partners stand to see faster processing and fewer filings, with the agency estimating about 245 fewer license applications during the one-year pause. Companies that work with Arrow China Electronics Trading Co., Ltd. may find it easier to do business again now that the company is no longer on the restricted list. Clarifying the aliases associated with Arrow Electronics (Hong Kong) Co., Ltd. should also reduce confusion about which names are still restricted, improving compliance and planning for many firms.

Who might be negatively affected? Competitors that benefited from stricter limits could face renewed competition. Some national security advocates may worry that easing controls, even narrowly, could carry risk. Compliance teams will also need to adjust quickly: the change was issued without a public comment period, and the lighter paperwork burden is temporary, with requirements scheduled to return on November 10, 2026. It’s also important to note that Arrow Electronics (Hong Kong) Co., Ltd. remains on the restricted list, and transactions involving that entity are still subject to strict review.

Overall, the move signals a targeted recalibration rather than a broad shift. It offers near-term relief and clarity for many businesses, while keeping key restrictions in place and leaving room for future rulemaking based on additional public input.
